stances.claim: Law journals develop a fundamentally different capability from bar-exam mastery -- bar success rewards memorizing definitions, enumerations, and quotations 'till the words are erased from the pages,' while journal editing and writing trains analysis, criticism, and elegant innovation.

The 'legal technician' interprets law literally to serve commercial and pecuniary causes; the 'social engineer' interprets law liberally and treats it as 'an instrument in the building of a just society,' a brick in the social edifice rather than an end in itself.

CJ Teehankee is the model of both -- summa cum laude, bar topnotcher, and social engineer who reached for justice 'via the all-encompassing rule of law' -- proving the two modes are complementary, not exclusive.
stances.rhetorical_move: exemplar-as-synthesis (the named hero embodying the dual mastery)

stances.claim: FLP, like the Claudio Teehankee Foundation, exists precisely to cultivate the social-engineer disposition through scholarships (20 at ₱200,000/year), honor-grad rewards (₱25,000-₱100,000), and dissertation writing contests (25 prizes of ₱20,000-₱300,000) -- explicitly recognizing 'elegant masterpieces composed mostly by law journal editors and writers.'
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-program announcement disguised as tribute close

notable_anecdotes: The bar-reviewer's aphorism -- 'you must read and reread and reread the Constitution, the codes, the Rules of Court and all the damn statutes over and over, over and over till the words are erased from the pages' -- quoted as a vivid period-piece illustration of what bar-exam mastery requires (and implicitly, what it does not develop).

The lawyer-character listing as a quiet jab -- 'best practicing lawyers are not the obnoxious charlatans who try to impress with highfalutin irrelevancies' but are 'tireless writers of term sheets, memoranda, contracts, treaties, complaints, answers, motions, briefs and memorials' -- the most explicit and longest CJ enumeration of what good practice consists of in this set of columns.

The Teehankee verdict in three compressed phrases -- 'He was a social engineer who reached out to the stars to render justice via the all-encompassing rule of law' -- the column's emotional and rhetorical apex.

The FLP-program announcement folded into the tribute close -- 20 scholarships of ₱200,000, honor-grad rewards ₱25,000-₱100,000, and 25 dissertation prizes ranging ₱20,000-₱300,000 -- explicit fundraising-and-recruitment messaging delivered in the homage register.

one_paragraph_summary: Marking CJ Claudio Teehankee's 100th-birthday year, Panganiban delivers excerpts from his July 10, 2019 speech launching the Ateneo Law Journal's hardcover special edition. He praises journal editors and writers as the analytical engine of the legal profession -- distinct from bar-exam toppers, whose mastery is memorizational ('read and reread and reread... till the words are erased from the pages'). The best practicing lawyers, he writes, are not the 'obnoxious charlatans who try to impress with highfalutin irrelevancies' but the 'tireless writers of term sheets, memoranda, contracts, treaties, complaints, answers, motions, briefs and memorials,' and the best jurists are 'rippling authors of decisions and orders.' He sets out his organizing typology: the 'legal technician' interprets law literally to serve commercial causes, while the 'social engineer' interprets law liberally, treating it as 'an instrument in the building of a just society' -- a brick in the social edifice rather than an end in itself. Teehankee, summa cum laude and bar topnotcher, was both -- 'a social engineer who reached out to the stars to render justice via the all-encompassing rule of law.' He closes with an announcement of FLP's programs: 20 annual law scholarships at ₱200,000 each, honor-grad rewards of ₱25,000-₱100,000, and 25 dissertation-writing contest prizes ranging ₱20,000-₱300,000 -- funding 'elegant masterpieces composed mostly by law journal editors and writers' to grow the next generation of social engineers for the nation.
